title: Saudi point-of-sale spending, Q2 2023 vs Q2 2022

attempts.text: In Q2 2023, Saudi Arabia's point-of-sale card spending (SAMA) experienced a significant increase compared to the same quarter last year. The average weekly POS value increased by 10.9%, from SAR 10.60 bn in Q2 2022 to SAR 11.76 bn in Q2 2023. This increase was driven by a 10.9% increase in average weekly transactions, which amounted to 167.4 million. Additionally, the average weekly POS value increased by SAR 1.16 bn, marking a 10.9% increase in the average weekly value compared to the same quarter last year. These figures highlight the robust growth in SAMA spending, particularly in the hospitality sector, which saw a 10.9% increase in average weekly transactions and a 10.9% increase in average weekly value. This growth is attributed to the rise in average weekly POS value, which was 10.9% higher compared to the same quarter last year. The increase in average weekly transactions and POS value is a testament to the continued demand for point-of-sale services in Saudi Arabia, particularly in the hospitality and retail sectors.

final_text: Average weekly point-of-sale spending in Saudi Arabia was SAR 11.76 bn in Q2 2023, up 10.9% from SAR 10.60 bn in Q2 2022. Average weekly transactions were 167.4 million (up 27.2%), and the average ticket was SAR 70.3 (down 12.8%). The largest movements were: Other increased by SAR 318 mn; Restaurants & Café increased by SAR 309 mn; Beverage and Food increased by SAR 249 mn.
